$comment: 38-question Q&A eval set for the Cortex Engineering Brain, rebuilt on 2026-08-02 against the current o8 tree, git history, ~/.o8 directives, and ~/.o8/cortex-ide.db. Every case records an independently re-derivable sourceOfTruth. The answer key was not derived through o8 ask, cortex_ask, or any other Brain surface. Category counts remain 5 each for ownership, decisions, processes, incidents, specs, and cross-repo, plus 8 literal-lookup cases.

cases.question: Which seeded directives are scoped specifically to the o8 repo, and which seeded directives are global?
cases.expectedAnswer: Six seeded directives are repo-scoped to o8: the 800-line file ceiling, glass-chrome-preserved, inline-styles-only, no-native-form-controls-in-packets, palette-vars, and phosphor-svg-only directives. Two seeded directives are global: typecheck-before-commit and surgical-changes.
expectedFacts: Names the six repo-scoped seeded directives
Identifies repoName o8 for the repo-scoped seeds
Identifies typecheck-before-commit and surgical-changes as global

cases.question: Which project contains the o8 repo, and which repositories are registered in that project as of the 2026-08-02 ground-truth rebuild?
cases.expectedAnswer: o8 belongs to the o8 project (slug o8, id proj-5d0d9e02-015). The project contains nine registered repos: o8, o8-site, o8-mobile, o8-license-server, o8-relay, ginsu, o8-business, o8-security, and matori.
cases.sourceOfTruth: ~/.o8/cortex-ide.db projects row id=proj-5d0d9e02-015 and project_repos rows project_id=proj-5d0d9e02-015; ~/.o8/projects.json:4-16
expectedFacts: Names the o8 project and id proj-5d0d9e02-015
States that the project contains nine registered repos
Names o8-site, o8-mobile, o8-license-server, o8-relay, ginsu, o8-business, o8-security, and matori

cases.question: Which registered repository is the main repo for the o8 project?
cases.expectedAnswer: The o8 project's main_repo_id is 70954348-8e56-41dd-ac10-5b4e91964fc2, which maps to the registered repo named o8.
expectedFacts: Names main_repo_id 70954348-8e56-41dd-ac10-5b4e91964fc2
Maps that repository id to o8

cases.question: Which directories own orchestrator backend selection and worker runtime execution, and can those two roles use different systems for one turn?
cases.expectedAnswer: Orchestrator backends live in src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/ and decide which system drives an orchestration turn. Worker/runtime adapters live in src/lib/runtimes/ and normalize worker execution behind the runtime registry and capability contract. The active orchestrator and dispatched worker can be different systems.
expectedFacts: Names src/lib/lane/orchestrator-backends/
Names src/lib/runtimes/
States that orchestrator backend and worker runtime are independent

cases.question: Which directive owner enforces the rule that packet metadata rows cannot use native select or input controls?
cases.expectedAnswer: The seed-cortex-ide-no-native-form-controls-in-packets directive owns the rule. It is scoped to repoName o8 at priority 7 and points to ThoughtsMissionPanel and the packet-meta-rows pattern as the examples to copy.
expectedFacts: Names seed-cortex-ide-no-native-form-controls-in-packets
Identifies repoName o8 and priority 7
Mentions ThoughtsMissionPanel and packet-meta-rows

cases.question: Why does o8 forbid CSS classes and require inline styles?
cases.expectedAnswer: iOS Safari and the Tauri webview have shipped reliability issues with class-based styling. The inline-styles-only directive makes this a permanent reliability rule: JSX styling belongs in style={{ }} props, with React.CSSProperties used for vendor-prefixed or non-standard properties.
expectedFacts: Names iOS Safari and the Tauri webview as the reliability driver
Identifies the rule as permanent
Requires style props and allows React.CSSProperties for non-standard properties

cases.question: Why are React icon component imports (lucide-react, @phosphor-icons/react) banned in favor of raw SVG?
cases.expectedAnswer: The React icon components do not render correctly inside the Tauri webview, so the phosphor-svg-only directive requires raw SVG path data from @phosphor-icons/react/dist/defs/. The src/lib/icons/ shim covers 85 common icons, and trivial actions should use HTML entities.
expectedFacts: Names Tauri webview rendering as the cause
Mentions @phosphor-icons/react/dist/defs/
Mentions the 85-icon src/lib/icons/ shim

cases.question: When Cortex memory conflicts with the current repository, what wins, and what provenance and failure rules constrain the answer?
cases.expectedAnswer: Current repository state outranks stale memory. Synthesized answers retain inspectable citations and explicit project scope. Missing or malformed indexes fail closed or degrade to narrower retrieval; they never manufacture evidence, and memory cannot bypass tests, principal checks, or approval gates.
expectedFacts: States that current repository state outranks stale memory
Requires inspectable citations and explicit project scope
States that missing indexes fail closed or degrade without manufacturing evidence
States that memory cannot bypass tests or approval gates

cases.question: Why is o8-site deployed as a web project while the o8 repository is not?
cases.expectedAnswer: o8 is a Tauri v2 desktop application that packages the web frontend, a local Next.js server, the WebSocket bridge, native helpers, and the o8 CLI into native builds. o8-site is the standalone web surface and is the project's Vercel deployment.
expectedFacts: Identifies o8 as a Tauri desktop application
Mentions the packaged local Next.js server and WebSocket bridge
Identifies o8-site as the web deployment

cases.question: When can a worker runtime use a declarative catalog entry, and when does the runtime contract require a specialized adapter?
cases.expectedAnswer: A CLI with argv-based launch or resume and line, JSONL, or NDJSON output can use one declarative catalog entry. Setting resumeArgs to null declares a truthful one-shot runtime. Stateful process control that cannot be expressed through argv and output patterns, such as bidirectional permission responses, requires a specialized owned-session adapter and AgentRuntime registration.
expectedFacts: Allows a declarative entry for argv-based launch or resume with line-oriented output
States that null resumeArgs means one-shot
Requires a specialized adapter for stateful or bidirectional process control

cases.question: What is the required local check before every commit?
cases.expectedAnswer: Run npx tsc --noEmit before every commit. The global typecheck directive marks this as mandatory on shared codebases; npm run typecheck is the fuller Next.js variant that regenerates types before TypeScript runs.
expectedFacts: Names npx tsc --noEmit
States that it is mandatory before every commit
Mentions npm run typecheck as the fuller Next.js variant

cases.question: What is the default file-size ceiling, and which files are currently waived?
cases.expectedAnswer: The default ceiling is 800 lines. The current mechanical waivers are src/app/dashboard/page.tsx, src/ws-server.ts, src/lib/worktree/manager.ts, and src/lib/lane/commands.ts. A new waiver requires an explicit user decision.
expectedFacts: States the 800-line default ceiling
Names all four current waivers
States that new waivers require an explicit user decision

cases.question: What is the surgical-changes rule for this codebase?
cases.expectedAnswer: Every changed line must trace back to the request. Do not improve or refactor adjacent code, comments, or formatting; match the existing style and report unrelated cleanup opportunities instead of silently rewriting them.
expectedFacts: States that every changed line traces to the request
Forbids adjacent refactors and formatting cleanup
Requires reporting unrelated opportunities instead of silently changing them

cases.question: What command sequence does the guarded daily-driver release loop use for o8?
cases.expectedAnswer: Use Node 22, run npm version patch so sync-version.mjs updates package.json, src-tauri/tauri.conf.json, and src-tauri/Cargo.toml and creates the version tag; run git push --follow-tags; then run npm run ship to build the signed app and upload the release assets. The installed app's UpdateCard discovers and verifies the signed update.
expectedFacts: Requires Node 22
Names npm version patch and the three synchronized manifests
Names git push --follow-tags
Names npm run ship and the signed update flow

cases.question: What decision ladder does the current default-deny API middleware apply to an /api request?
cases.expectedAnswer: The middleware first permits narrowly defined self-authenticating routes whose handlers verify their own credentials, then checks read-only and any-method allowlists, then trusted loopback, then a ws-token or active device bearer. Requests that match none of those paths return 401. There is no fail-open gated-prefix list.
expectedFacts: States that the API is default-deny
Orders self-authenticating routes, allowlists, loopback, and bearer fallback
States that unmatched requests return 401
States that there is no fail-open gated-prefix list

cases.question: What failure caused the glass-chrome-preserved directive to be added?
cases.expectedAnswer: A blanket replacement of low-opacity rgba whites with solid palette tokens collapsed the macOS vibrancy chrome into opaque blobs. Those translucent whites are intentional tints on the surrounding chrome, while workspace, chat, and terminal surfaces are intentionally solid, so rgba sweeps must be visually verified instead of applied wholesale.
expectedFacts: States that low-opacity rgba whites were replaced wholesale
Explains that glass chrome collapsed into opaque blobs
Distinguishes glass chrome from intentionally solid content surfaces
Requires visual verification before rgba sweeps

cases.question: Which packet finished only partial, and what work was left over?

expectedFacts: Names feat/packet-meta-rows-restyle
States outcome partial
Identifies runtime and summary rows as the leftover work
Mentions the native-select-to-popover follow-up

cases.question: Why did the orchestrator-empty-state-copy outcome get flagged by the reviewer even though it shipped?
cases.expectedAnswer: The polish/orchestrator-empty-state-copy outcome rewrote the empty-state copy and quick-action card layout. The reviewer flagged the new copy as off-brand relative to the locked design language.

Mentions the empty-state copy and quick-action layout rewrite

cases.question: Did the first o8_view webview-tool attempts ship cleanly, and what failed?
cases.expectedAnswer: No. Outcome so-1776188979528-a3yz23te added and wired the client and tools but went idle between runs before a clean commit. Outcome so-1776188344936-92de5fx8 tried to expose tool availability in diagnostics, but git refused the commit because only an unrelated settings file appeared modified.
expectedFacts: Identifies both failed outcome ids
Mentions the idle-between-runs failure
Mentions git refusing the diagnostics commit because only an unrelated settings file was modified

cases.question: Which browser API assumption crashed the dashboard in v0.1.252, and what guard pattern prevents a repeat?
cases.expectedAnswer: The macOS WKWebView did not implement window.requestIdleCallback or window.cancelIdleCallback even though TypeScript's DOM types allowed them. Unguarded mount-time calls in footer-ports and supervisor-inbox-badge crashed the dashboard in v0.1.252; v0.1.253 hotfixed the failure. Callers must feature-detect with typeof ... === 'function' and use a setTimeout or no-op fallback.
expectedFacts: Names requestIdleCallback and cancelIdleCallback as absent
States that unguarded mount-time calls crashed v0.1.252
Names v0.1.253 as the hotfix
Requires typeof function guards and a fallback

cases.question: Which evidence inputs does the current Cortex memory specification index?
cases.expectedAnswer: Cortex indexes repository documentation, operator-authored directives and accepted rules, completed session outcomes plus review and approval history, structured project and repository records, and facts extracted by the distillation pipeline. Source identity remains attached to each record.
expectedFacts: Names repository documentation
Names directives and accepted rules
Names completed outcomes, reviews, and approvals
Names project/repository records and distilled facts
States that source identity stays attached

cases.question: Which agent and squad statuses does the fleet-state specification define?
cases.expectedAnswer: Agent statuses are idle, running, waiting, reviewing, blocked, and failed. Squad statuses are healthy, watching, degraded, and blocked. The shared vocabulary lets desktop, mobile, and runtime adapters distinguish execution, expected waiting, review bottlenecks, recoverable intervention, and terminal failure.
expectedFacts: Names all six agent statuses
Names all four squad statuses
Explains that the status vocabulary is shared across surfaces

cases.question: Which Tauri surface and label does the native-browser specification require, and which Tauri surface does it reject?
cases.expectedAnswer: The spec requires a stable child WebviewWindow labeled browser-view. The native host injects and evaluates the page agent in that owned window so it can drive the DOM across origins. It rejects Tauri multiwebview because that API is unstable and has positioning, resize, focus, and child-selection blockers.
expectedFacts: Requires a child WebviewWindow
Names the browser-view label
Rejects Tauri multiwebview
Explains that host-owned eval provides DOM access across origins

cases.question: Where do managed worktrees default today, how is that root overridden, and what legacy layout is still discovered?
cases.expectedAnswer: Managed worktrees default to ~/.o8/worktrees/<repo-key>/.cortex-worktrees/. O8_WORKTREE_ROOT overrides the root. src/lib/worktree/root-layout.ts still discovers repository-local .cortex-worktrees/ stores for backward compatibility.
expectedFacts: Names ~/.o8/worktrees/<repo-key>/.cortex-worktrees/
Names O8_WORKTREE_ROOT
Mentions repository-local .cortex-worktrees/ backward compatibility

cases.question: What structural contract does validate:qa-cases enforce, and which dimensions does the judge score?
cases.expectedAnswer: The validator requires at least 30 cases, exactly five cases in each of the six seeded categories, allows literal-lookup as the seventh category, validates required fields and repo-path resolution, and warns rather than fails when live citation rows are absent. The judge scores factual_accuracy, citation_correctness, and hallucination_count.
expectedFacts: Names at least 30 total cases
Names exactly five per seeded category
Names literal-lookup as the seventh allowed category
Names repo-path validation and citation warnings
Names factual_accuracy, citation_correctness, and hallucination_count
